headline: Approved up to $43,500,000 in bonds for a Public Works garage and fleet facility, plus pool repairs, and an $11,692,041.56 wastewater plant upgrade contract.
summary: Members heard an introduction from the new Greeley Park Advisory Committee and received a Director's Report. Approved bond measures for sewer, wastewater, solid waste, pool, and garage projects, plus wastewater and Eversource contracts and a drainlayer's license.
decisions: Approved borrowing an additional $345,000.00 from the Clean Water State Revolving Fund for the Four Hills Landfill PFAS/Leachate Removal and Destruction Pilot Test Program; motion carried unanimously.

Approved R-26-059, authorizing the Mayor and City Treasurer to borrow up to $3,000,000.00 through bonds and/or a state loan for the Wastewater Treatment Plant Phase 1 Upgrades Project; motion carried unanimously.
Approved R-26-060, authorizing bonds not to exceed $4,275,000.00 for the City's sewer infrastructure improvement and sewer and drain casting replacement programs; motion carried unanimously.
Approved R-26-061, authorizing bonds not to exceed $2,550,000.00 for various wastewater capital improvements; motion carried unanimously.
Approved R-26-063, authorizing bonds not to exceed $2,678,828.00 for the purchase of Solid Waste capital equipment; motion carried unanimously.
Approved R-26-063 again, as listed in a second entry for the same bond purchase of Solid Waste capital equipment not to exceed $2,678,828.00; motion carried unanimously.
Approved R-26-066, authorizing bonds not to exceed $5,000,000.00 for the repair and renovation of two public inground swimming pools; motion carried unanimously.

Approved R-26-072, authorizing bonds not to exceed $43,500,000.00 for the design, construction and equipping of a Division of Public Works Garage and Fleet Maintenance Facility; motion carried unanimously.
Approved R-26-073, changing the purpose of up to $3,183,200.00 of unexpended bond proceeds to the Division of Public Works Garage and Fleet Maintenance Facility Project; motion carried unanimously.
Approved the user warrants as presented; motion carried unanimously.
Approved a work agreement with Eversource, not to exceed $29,595.02, for replacement of city-owned electrical equipment on Eversource-owned poles; motion carried unanimously.

Approved a contract with Loureiro Building Construction, LLC of Plainville, Connecticut, not to exceed $11,692,041.56, for the Phase I Upgrade Project, pending bond approval; motion carried unanimously.
Approved a contract with Wright Pierce of Thompson, Maine, not to exceed $1,361,000.00, for construction administration services for the Phase I Upgrade Project; motion carried unanimously.
Approved the sewer service permits and fees as submitted; motion carried unanimously.
Approved a drainlayer's license for Valor Excavation, LLC of Pelham, New Hampshire, with a temporary suspension option during an initial 6-month probationary period; motion carried unanimously.
Considered Liberty Utilities' request to modify the required moratorium restoration on Northeastern Boulevard, which would limit milling to one lane, about 150 feet; motion carried unanimously.
Approved and unsealed the non-public personnel minutes from the August 27, 2026 meeting; motion carried unanimously.
Accepted the resignation of Michael Dube Jr., Parks, effective September 18, 2026; motion carried unanimously.
Voted 3-0 by roll call to seal the minutes of the September 24, 2026 non-public personnel meeting until a majority of the Board votes that confidentiality is no longer needed.

MEETING OF THE BOARD OF PUBLIC WORKS 
September 24, 2026 
Approved - MEETING MINUTES 
 
A meeting of the Board of Public Works was held on September 24, 2026 at 4:00 p.m., at the 
Division of Public Works Administration Building in the Mine Falls Conference Room, 848 West 
Hollis Street, Nashua, New Hampshire 03062.   
 
Chairman, James Donchess, Mayor, declared the meeting to order at 4:00 p.m. and called the 
roll.   
 
I. ROLL CALL 
 
Members Present:      Members Absent:  
 
Chairman, James Donchess, Mayor    Vice-Chairman, Matthew Gregg 
Commissioner, Manny Espitia    Commissioner, June Lemen 
Commissioner, Paul Shea     Clerk, Lisa Fauteux 
 
Also Present: 
 
Michael B. O'Brien, Sr., Aldermanic Liaison 
Carolyn O'Connor, Assistant Director of PW Finance & Administration 
Kathleen Roddy, Member Greeley Park Advisory Committee 
Francis Murphy, Chairman, Greeley Park Advisory Committee 
David Boucher, Superintendent, Wastewater 
Dan Hudson, P.E., City Engineer 
Anthony Beland, Liberty Utilities 
Jeff lLafleur, Superintendent Solid Waste 
 
II. MOTION:  TO APPROVE THE AGENDA AS SUBMITTED 
 
Chairman, James Donchess, Mayor 
 
Alright, so the first item is the Agenda.  Commissioner Shea.   
 
Motion by Commissioner Shea: To Approve The Agenda.   
 
MOTION CARRIED: Unanimously   
 
III. MOTION:  TO APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE BOARD OF PUBIC WORKS 
MEETING OF AUGUST 27, 2026.   
 
Chairman, James Donchess, Mayor 
 
Next is approving the minutes of the last meeting.  Commissioner Espitia.   
 
Motion by Commissioner Espitia: To Approve The Minutes Of The Board Of Public Works 
Meeting Of August 27, 2026.   
 
MOTION CARRIED: Unanimously
_____________________________________________________________________________________________
Board of Public Works Meeting of September 24, 2026  Page 2 of 22 
IV. PUBLIC COMMENT 
 
Chairman, James Donchess, Mayor 
 
Public Comment.  Is there any member of the public who wants to address the Board of Public 
Works?  I don't see anyone.  Okay.   
 
V. INTRODUCTION:  GREELEY PARK ADVISORY COMMITTEE 
 
Chairman, James Donchess, Mayor 
 
We do have the Greeley Park Advisory Committee.  Do we have people from that?  Yes.  We 
have a microphone over there.   
 
Kathleen Roddy, Member, Greeley Park Advisory Committee 
 
Do you want to start, or do you want me to? 
 
Francis Murphy, Chairman, Greeley Park Advisory Committee 
 
If you'd like to.  Yeah, sure.   
 
Mayor Donchess 
 
You should probably move the mic closer to you--your're on TV, so you know.   
 
Ms. Roddy 
 
My name is Kathleen Roddy, and I am a member of the Greeley Park Advisory Commission.  
Fran Murphy here to my left is the Chairperson, Chairman, and we wanted to come before the 
Department of Public Works to tell you that this is a new commission.  It started this year.  We 
have begun meeting, and so this is really just an introductory meeting for us to tell you who we 
are and what we're doing, and all of you know a lot of the history about Greeley Park.  We've 
been digging into that a little bit more.  The park is used by many people, not just Ward 3, I did 
an informal survey just the other day and walked through the park, and there were people from 
other towns using the park, as you all know.  You are truly the public servants in taking care of 
all of our public facilities and our parks.  This park has an amazing history, and what we'd like to 
do as part of the Commission is make sure that we preserve it for future generations.  Part of 
that is going to be working on a master plan.  We'd also like to take the opportunity to start 
some marketing on social media about the park.  When you start to dig into who Joseph 
Thornton Greeley was, why the park was given, there's a lot of fun facts there that people don't 
know about the park.  We thought we would start a Facebook page for Greeley.  One of the 
other people on the Commission, Allison Galipeau is going to work with me on that, and we 
thought we'd do some facts about the park because people are interested in it.  It's one of most 
historic pieces of land in the City.  We also wanted to be able to inform the public of things that 
are going on in the park, so it's not just left to Parks and Rec or DPW; we can be a little bit of a 
helping hand in that matter.  For example, if there are people complaining about the size of the 
plots, garden plots, perhaps the Commission can make a recommendation.  Perhaps that can 
then be referred to: okay, well we understand you'd rather have a 40 x 60 piece of land for your 
garden, but the Commission has recommended XYZ, and we're going to take that under 
advisement, or we're going to put that rule in place for the park.  We want to be able to establish
_____________________________________________________________________________________________
Board of Public Works Meeting of September 24, 2026  Page 3 of 22 
a level of communication with DPW so that the Commission knows when certain activities are 
planned in the park or things that are going to be done, the schedule for redoing the pool for 
instance, and we can get that word out on our social media.  One of the Commission members I 
just mentioned, Allison, who will be working on Facebook, has had this obsession with the 
stonehouse and that being the nicest bathrooms ever for a long time, and she would like to do a 
campaign: show us your prom pictures, show us your wedding pictures, things like that.  I don't 
know if we'll do a Throwback Thursday or a Fun Fact Friday, something like that, but it's a 
fascinating parcel of land, and we need to take care of it for future generations.  People sat 
around the table just like this in the same positions; I think it was then called the Parks 
Commission then, and they debated the same things back in the early 1900s after Greeley 
passed and the land was deeded to the City through the stipulations of his will.  There was a lot 
of issue getting money to do anything with that parcel, and it was a farm that was such a part of 
the town's history that Charlie would go up there and stop at it; there was an old tea house next 
to it where there are now a couple of million-dollar houses.  The people used the park from the 
very beginning once there was a master plan in place.  Now, there was some rumor that the 
park was actually had something, some connection to the Olmstead Farm, which was passed 
down to Ohm stead's sons.  I haven't found any evidence of that, but we are continuing to dig.  
When you get even just a little bit west of here, there are parks that do not have this kind of 
history.  So, that big giant boulder that's on the knoll that right now is surrounded by trees that 
nobody can see-- when you go back through the issues of the Nashua Telegraph in the 1800s, 
the people were fascinated by it then, and they loved this--there was one of the citizens who 
paid to get an 8-ton boulder, and how they got it up that knoll with horses is amazing to me, but 
they wanted to mark where there's a burial ground.  People have been fascinated with that for 
hundreds of years, so they think that there are--the last body was buried there in the early 
1800s, and there are people from the 1600s and 1700s possibly buried there.  Somewhere in 
the realm between 90 and 120 souls from what I've been able to dig up.  So again, these are all 
amazing historical facts, and they're kind of being hidden in the park.  What the Commission 
would like to do is be part of working on a master plan for the park so that we can preserve it, so 
that if we need to plant some more trees or things need to be adjusted for safety purposes or--if 
you're on Manchester Street, you don't know unless you're probably in this room--you don't 
know that you can go from Manchester Street to the Merrimack River through the park.  And we 
would just like to be part of the discussions with DPW about the park, and part of the master 
planning with Director Sullivan, and you will start to see some of our social media campaign, 
and any time that we can partner with you on anything, we would like to do so.  That is really 
just what I wanted to say today.  Thank you.   
 
Mayor Donchess 
 
Well, thank you very much for all your efforts.  Going back to the beginning, you were talking 
about how many people do visit the park.  We do have this place or AI service, which uses cell 
phone data to determine how many people have been in a particular area during a particular 
time, and we either reviewed Greeley for the calendar year 24 or 25; I can't remember which, 
but we can renew this.  It was 90,000 visits, and you can determine where the people came 
from, and from Nashua.  There were a lot from the 03064 zip code.  You can't tell from what zip 
code they come from, but they were from all over Nashua, and a lot of people from out of 
Nashua, out of state, as you've already said.  We can get that renewed very easily, which I will 
take care of, but you know you are right that many, many people are visiting there every year.  
Compared with the same review, it showed 60,000 people at Mine Falls and 60,000 as well at 
Robbie Park.  Obviously, we're getting a lot of people at Greeley.
_____________________________________________________________________________________________
Board of Public Works Meeting of September 24, 2026  Page 4 of 22 
Ms. Roddy 
 
And I think you can all agree, each of our parks has a different sort of personality, a different 
flavor, and Greeley Park is for gathering.  There are people that gather there for a multitude of 
reasons, family events every day.  Senior citizens in their lawn chairs enjoying just a beautiful 
day out.  It's a different park than anything else, and it's extremely historical, so we definitely 
want to make sure that the public knows more about history because I am just an average 
person, and the more I started digging into it, it was truly fascinating, and all the connections 
that the Greeley family has to Nashua in the area.  The wars that they served in, the companies 
that they served on and ran, are fascinating.  I think other people will find that fascinating too, 
and our hope is that with that sort of marketing campaign we will then be able to generate some 
public interest when it does come time to do a little bit of planning for the park, and keeping up 
some of the necessary work that needs to happen there.   
 
Mayor Donchess 
 
Alright, do the Commissioners have any questions or comments or anything?   
 
Commissioner Paul Shea 
 
First, thank you for your love for Greeley Park and for watching over it and wanting to celebrate 
it, and celebrating it.  There's absolutely a lot of fascinating history there.  At one point, I did 
some light art scans of the park just to see what was out there, and there are some old building 
foundations, I understand, and lots of fascinating little things.  Have you come across the--they 
used to do, I want to say in the 1900s, teens they used to do late-night celebrations out there 
with a bonfire and dancing and all sorts of things.  Very fascinating stuff, and it's a beautiful 
space.  The boulder is very interesting too.  Do you have the names of the people that are out 
there?   
 
Ms. Roddy 
 
Most of the people that were buried there--the records are probably with Dunstable.  It wasn't 
Nashua then.  But a man named Ira Harris, who worked at Indian Head Bank, some of his 
ancestors were buried there, and I believe in the 1900s teens, I want to say it was 1915 or so, 
he was the one that paid to have the boulder there to commemorate all of the souls that were 
buried there because they were some of the first settlers in Nashua, and what I read in the 
paper was that it was the first burial ground north of the Nashua River.  Now, at the time that 
those people were buried there, the graves were only marked with stones, not gravestones just 
literal just rocks, head and toe.  One of the military units used to have their drills at the park 
back when it was Greeley Farm, and at one point they were--I don't know they were camping 
there for a certain amount of time, and they took all the stones and used them for their oven and 
their fire.  So people got really upset that those graves were being disturbed.  There were tenant 
farms before it became the park.  So, some of the bodies actually got tugged up, but most of 
them are buried on that knoll and beneath it.   
 
Commissioner Shea 
 
And I didn't know that that was the nature of the stone.  It's not very clear based on the plaque 
that that is what it's there for.
_____________________________________________________________________________________________
Board of Public Works Meeting of September 24, 2026  Page 5 of 22 
Ms. Roddy 
 
Right.   
 
Commissioner Shea 
 
Whether it be a plaque with names, if those are available or some other signifier with 
information for people to know about the history of that space, that would be really nice too.   
 
Ms. Roddy 
 
We are definitely looking into that, and a lot of people on the Commission have ties into the 
Historical Society and other avenues to kind of get this data.  We're working on that-- 
 
Commissioner Shea 
 
--that's great-- 
 
Ms. Roddy 
 
--and that's what we'd like to communicate through social media, just to continue public interest 
in the park with the hope of us having a plan for keeping it up for future generations.  One quick 
other interesting fact I found out.  There was a judge I forgot his last name, Clyde something--
and he, at one point in the 1911 to I think it was 1920 in that time frame, he talked about getting 
together with people in Hudson, building a bridge from Greeley over to Hudson where they were 
going to build a horse track-- 
 
Commissioner Shea 
 
--oh, cool-- 
 
Ms. Roddy 
 
--because they wanted rival what was being built down in Boston, and it was the intention to 
have this whole big entertainment complex there.  It's just interesting what, over time, people 
thought that they would want to do with the park and what it actually came to be.  I think other 
people will find that interesting.   
 
Commissioner Shea 
 
I wonder if those bridge pillars that are out there, I think those are kind of in line with Greeley; 
I'm not 100 percent.  There's two old bridge pillars just south of the bridge across to Hudson, 
and it seems like they might be at about that point, but I don't know. I don't want to get too far 
ahead of myself, but I see those; I go out there on a boat sometimes with a friend.  We live over 
by the boat ramp, and I'm down there all the time, kind of just checking out the river and 
enjoying the woods, but sometimes out on the water, and I see those pillars, and I wonder if 
something, a pedestrian something, someday might be possible for that, but anyway, that's way 
far down the road, if ever.  But, anyway, thank you for what you're doing and thank you for 
coming and sharing with us today.
_____________________________________________________________________________________________
Board of Public Works Meeting of September 24, 2026  Page 6 of 22 
Ms. Roddy 
 
I do, I want to also thank Superintendent Conant and Director Fauteux; they've been part of our 
Commission, and I just appreciate their involvement and communication.  So, we'd like to foster 
continued communication with Parks and Rec. and DPW.  Thank you.   
 
Mayor Donchess 
 
Commissioner Espitia.   
 
Commissioner Manny Espitia 
 
I’m very excited about the post for the bathroom because the number of folks I've seen take 
photos there.  I took my wedding invitation photos there with my wife, so-- 
 
Ms. Roddy 
 
--well, that's great.  We would like to feature your photos.   
 
Commissioner Espitia 
 
I mean, it's great.  It was during COVID too so that was fun.  The park was really empty.  I think 
the number of--the amount of programming that's been done at that park, I think 100 percent 
you guys encapsulated when you say that it is a meeting space.  I would love to see the idea of 
having it have a master plan, and making sure it continues to be fostered as a place where 
people can meet.   
 
Ms. Roddy 
 
Excellent, thank you.   
 
Mayor Donchess 
 
Alright, well, thanks for coming in and updating us.  If you need anything, you can always come 
back.   
 
Ms. Roddy 
 
Thank you very much.
